intro: This branch studies conic sections: the curves made by slicing a cone, namely circles, ellipses (ovals), parabolas and hyperbolas. They describe planet orbits, satellite dishes and headlights, and a few skills ask the learner to put the steps of a short derivation in order.

V.12.01.what: The four conic curves all come from slicing a double cone (two cones tip to tip) with a flat plane at different tilts.

levels.a: Sees that a cut straight across the cone makes a circle.
levels.b: Sees that a cut less steep than the cone's sides makes an ellipse (an oval).
levels.c: Tells a parabola from a hyperbola by comparing the cut's tilt with the cone's sides.
levels.d: Names any slice, including special cuts through the tip that give a point, a line or two crossing lines.

V.12.02.what: A parabola is every point the same distance from a fixed point (the focus) and a fixed line (the directrix).

levels.a: Uses the equal-distance rule to find a point on a parabola.
levels.b: Puts in order the steps that turn the equal-distance rule into an equation.
levels.c: Finds the focus and directrix from an equation.
levels.d: Finds the number p, the distance from the turning point to the focus, after rearranging the equation.
levels.e: Finds a point's distance to the focus quickly by measuring to the directrix instead.
levels.f: Works with a line through the focus, finding one end's distance from the other's.

V.12.03.what: Writing and reading parabola equations that open up, down, left or right.

levels.a: Finds the focus of a parabola that opens up or down.
levels.b: Finds the focus of a parabola that opens left or right.
levels.c: Writes the equation from the turning point and the focus or directrix.
levels.d: Picks the graph that matches an equation.

V.12.04.what: An ellipse is every point whose distances to two fixed points (the foci) add up to the same total.

levels.a: Uses the constant total to find a missing distance to a focus.
levels.b: Connects this to drawing an ellipse with a loop of string around two pins.
levels.c: Reads the lengths of the long and short axes from an equation.
levels.d: Finds the eccentricity, a number saying how stretched the oval is.

levels.a: Writes the standard equation from the center and the ends of the axes.
levels.b: Tells whether the ellipse is wide or tall from its equation.
levels.c: Picks the graph that matches an equation.
levels.d: Writes the equation of an ellipse from its graph.

V.12.06.what: Locating the two foci of an ellipse and using them in real settings.

levels.a: Finds the distance from the center to each focus with a Pythagoras-like rule.
levels.b: Finds the coordinates of both foci.
levels.c: Uses foci to explain whispering galleries, where a whisper at one focus is heard at the other.
levels.d: Works out how stretched a planet's orbit is from its closest and farthest distances.
levels.e: Works backwards from the foci and one point on the curve to write the equation.
levels.f: Finds the area of the triangle formed by a point on the ellipse and the two foci.

V.12.07.what: A hyperbola is every point whose distances to two foci differ by the same amount. It has two separate branches.

levels.a: Uses the constant difference to find a missing distance to a focus.
levels.b: Finds the vertices (turning points) from an equation.
levels.c: Finds the distance from the center to each focus.
levels.d: Finds the coordinates of both foci.

V.12.08.what: Writing and graphing hyperbola equations, using a guide box and slanted guide lines (asymptotes) the branches approach.

levels.a: Writes the standard equation from the center, a vertex and a focus.
levels.b: Puts in order a short proof that the guide box's corners are as far from the center as the foci.
levels.c: Finds the equations of the asymptotes.
levels.d: Picks the equation that matches a graph.

V.12.09.what: Telling which conic a general equation describes.

levels.a: Completes the square to rewrite an equation in standard form and find its center.
levels.b: Uses the signs and sizes of the x squared and y squared terms to name the conic.
levels.c: Calculates a test number (the discriminant) for equations with an xy term.
levels.d: Names the graph, including unusual cases such as two crossing lines or a single point.

V.12.10.what: Seeing conics at work in the real world.

levels.a: Finds the depth of a satellite dish with the receiver at its focus.
levels.b: Writes the shape of a headlight reflector, with the bulb at the focus.
levels.c: Uses eccentricity to find where a star sits in a planet's orbit.
levels.d: Uses signal timing from two radio stations (LORAN navigation) to locate a ship.

V.12.11.what: Finding where a conic meets a line or another conic by solving their equations together.

levels.a: Finds where a line crosses a parabola.
levels.c: Chooses substitution or elimination to solve a system.
levels.d: Works out how many crossing points there are.
levels.e: Finds the value that makes a line just touch a curve (be tangent to it).
levels.f: Finds which values of a changing number give exactly one meeting point.
